column1: # Feature-level P4 evidence anchors for the P5 three-axis ledger (G2 closure).
# One row per `(feature_id, frontend)`: the hand-declared behaviour test that
# backs the shape's delivery claim for that feature.  The anchor must be a real
# nextest test id, exactly as `cargo nextest list` reports it; the resolver
# fails the run when a referenced test is renamed or deleted.
#   feature_id  stable `FeatureId` id; the vocabulary authority is the Rust
#               contract test rejects an unknown id, mirroring `ContractTag`).
#   test_id     the nextest test path, or `-` on a pending row
#   note        `-` on an anchored row; the honest gap on a pending row
# Discipline (same as the facet manifest and the unified matrix):
#   * anchors are declared by hand and verified against discovery; a test id is
#     NEVER derived by scanning Rust source;
#   * `pending` is not a pass: it records that this `(feature, frontend)` pair
#     was surveyed and no discoverable behaviour test exists yet, so the folded
#     cell stays refused by G2 with this note as the recorded gap;
#   * a row absent from this table is simply not yet surveyed; `Ready` still
#     requires a committed anchor, so absence is never a silent delivery claim.
# First anchored batch (2026-09-22): the four features every frontend really
# renders and every Linux source lane registers as `Present` -
# `services.dependency-dag`.  The anchor proves the shape's delivered surface
# for that feature (the P1 semantic specification owns "what counts as
# delivered"; this table owns "a real test exists and resolves").
